description: A Late Iron Age settlement of the east bank of the Dubby Sike. A circular structure in the settlement was interpreted as a ring-cairn, with three shallow pits containing charcoal. This was interpreted as having a ceremonial purpose, and so the RSRB marks the site as a 'shrine'. It is thought that the settlement was only used in the summer months.
bibliography: Coffins, and Gidney. “A Late Prehistoric Site at Dubby Sike, Upper Teesdale, Co Durham.” Durham Archaeological Journal 4 (1988).
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Dubby Sike (Durham).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
